The global balance of power is shifting — and the Middle East is increasingly caught at the center.  
 In this edition of TV7 Powers in Play, Jonathan Hessen and a panel of Israeli security and strategic experts examine the evolving competition between the United States and China, Beijing’s calculations regarding Iran and Taiwan, Russia’s position amid the continuing war in Ukraine, and the growing strategic importance of the world’s critical maritime routes.

# Iran Wants Sanctions Eased to Allow Back Nuclear Inspectors

![Iran Wants Sanctions Eased to Allow Back Nuclear Inspectors](https://images.rigzone.com/images/news/articles/Iran-Wants-Sanctions-Eased-to-Allow-Back-Nuclear-Inspectors-184755-582x327.webp)

Iran's foreign minister suggested in private talks that his country was willing to restore nuclear inspectors' access to bombed facilities in exchange for sanctions relief, people familiar with the discussions said, a concession that could help break deadlocked peace talks with the US.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi raised the idea in meetings at the United Nations with European and Middle Eastern diplomats while he was in New York for the annual General Assembly, which ended earlier this week, according to the diplomats, who asked not to be identified discussing private deliberations.

He gave little away about the state of Iran's economy as a result of both sanctions and the US naval blockade outside the Strait of Hormuz that has choked off its oil exports. But his suggestion to counterparts that Iran would grant nuclear inspectors access in exchange for sanctions relief signals the extent of the country's economic pain, according to the diplomats.

Inflation in Iran is now almost 90 percent year over year, and the rial has weakened 30 percent against the dollar as sanctions begin to bite.

Araghchi also pressed Europeans to reverse a UN decision from last year to re-impose broad sanctions on Iran, a particular sore spot

October 2, 2026, 6:27 AM

# Turkey and UN Push Black Sea Truce to Protect Grain as Food Prices Climb

*Turkey and the United Nations are organizing new talks between Russia and Ukraine aimed at a Black Sea ceasefire focused on safeguarding grain exports as global food prices jump. The initiative tests whether wartime adversaries can ring‑fence a critical trade route feeding import‑dependent countries from North Africa to Asia.*

Escalating food costs are pulling the Black Sea war back to the negotiating table.

Turkey and the United Nations are arranging new talks between Russia and Ukraine for early October to discuss a ceasefire in the Black Sea designed specifically to protect grain shipments, according to a senior diplomat cited in reports. The aim is narrow but urgent: reduce the risk to commercial vessels carrying Ukrainian and Russian grain at a moment when world food prices are rising fast.

The planned meetings would revive a diplomatic track that has struggled since the collapse of the original Black Sea Grain Initiative, under which Moscow had allowed some Ukrainian agricultural exports to transit safely despite the broader conflict. This time, the focus is described as a ceasefire on the maritime front rather than a wider settlement, a recognition that both sides still see the land war as very much active.
